rules.statement: Do not invent content. Text, data, claims, features, people, quotes, logos and numbers that a person will read as fact ship only if the request, the approved layout or the existing page contains them; content already on a page does not exempt proof and claims from DEC-5. A request covers only its own content: placeholder rows or invented items inside a requested block are unrequested. Approval of a direction, a discussion or a reference unlocks proposals, not implementation. Each invented item in a delivered result is a finding; repeating it after a correction raises its severity. This rule is never a reason to remove parts of an existing page, such as its navigation, footer, actions, sections, illustrations or motifs; on an existing page, new elements, sections and decoration are proposed, not added (US-002). The visual treatment of requested content (type, color, motion, an illustration of the product) is design work judged by the interface rules, not by this one; sample data inside a product illustration is not a claim unless it presents customers, quotes or results as real. Not a finding: text the user supplied verbatim; the navigation, footer and primary action that a page of the requested kind needs, when their labels claim nothing the request lacks. Proposals and execution follow US-002.
rules.title: Ship only requested content

rules.statement: Follow the user's current explicit requirements when they differ from general style preferences. Review how well the requested design works and how it uses the project's design system. Do not reject an intentional choice merely because it appears in a generic anti-pattern list.
rules.title: Explicit requirements outrank generic style lists

rules.statement: When the agent believes an element outside the request is needed, it sends a separate proposal with the element's purpose and a preview instead of adding it to the result (UR-1). Inside the authorized scope, technical steps, checks and fixes of defects against the stated intent are done without asking, and signals such as risks, contradictions or lost elements are raised without asking. Outside that scope, or when a step is irreversible or external, the agent reports and asks first.
rules.title: Needed additions are proposed; execution is proactive

credits.work: Stageshow: references/review.md (The reviewer's brief); references/craft.md (Color and looks)

rules.statement: Before presenting a revision, verify the actual result against its requirements. Check design-system use, behavior and visual output separately. Reading guidelines or passing a build is not evidence that the interface meets its acceptance criteria. Use an independent reviewer before handoff. The reviewer gets the result and the original requirement, not the author's plan or explanations, and judges what is on screen. A finding is backed by a screenshot of the state it describes; a pass or a failure that is only expected, not seen, is not evidence. Each theme the product supports, such as light and dark, is checked on its own: a pass in one theme does not prove another.
rules.title: Verify the actual result before handoff

rules.statement: Make a systemic fix in the governing design-system component, token or recipe. Use its existing API or a defined extension, then verify the consuming interfaces. Do not conceal a local override behind a new token name.
rules.title: Fix systemic issues at the design-system source

rules.statement: A change to the design system does not by itself require renewed permission for work the user has already authorized. Ask when an unresolved product or design choice needs the owner's decision, and stay within the authorized scope.
rules.title: Design-system changes inside authorized work

rules.statement: Keep a project's visual recipes scoped to that project. Reuse the principle of consistency without turning a particular color, shape or treatment into a universal requirement.
rules.title: Visual recipes stay project-scoped

rules.statement: Preserve the provenance of examples, references and claimed results. Distinguish a recorded example from a live verified run, and an agent proposal from an owner-approved decision. State missing evidence explicitly.
rules.title: Keep provenance of examples and claims

rules.statement: Preserve approved content, behavior and composition outside the requested change. Compare the original requirement, the baseline and the candidate. Treat unverified areas as unknown rather than passed.
rules.title: Leave everything outside the change intact

rules.statement: When asked to remove a pattern throughout a product, locate and update every occurrence in the agreed scope. Verify the affected routes and components before handoff instead of fixing only the example that was pointed out.
rules.title: Product-wide removal covers every occurrence

rules.statement: A page that existed before the current task is the approved baseline for an audit or a fix of it (US-001, US-008). The typefaces, palette, motifs and motion it uses consistently, meaning the same treatment for the same role in two or more places or a reused class, token or component, count as its design system only where one of these rules makes an exception for the approved design system: decoration (DEC-1), lines (DEC-2), labels above headings (DEC-7) and monospace type (KR-19). Every other rule applies as written, with its own counter-examples. Only what is already on the page counts: the agent does not declare signatures, and an element it added, a one-off or an inconsistent use is judged by the rule as written. Repetition alone does not make a generic tell part of the baseline: a treatment that matches the Example of the rule it would be exempt from, or template decoration that would suit any site of the category, such as a background grid or scattered decorative squares, needs a design system documented in the project or the user's explicit requirement. A page generated in the current task is not a baseline. The baseline never covers these always-findings, which stay findings on any page and are fixed, not only reported: fabricated proof, numbers and promises (DEC-5); a pill or badge above the H1 (DEC-7); section or item numbering such as "01/" on elements that are not a real sequence (DEC-7); a sparkle, wand or gradient chip as a generic sign of AI (ST-2; the product's own registered icon excepted); claims about competitors without a verified source (XP-22b); agent or process service notes (US-009); placeholder or service text (XP-33); text contrast below WCAG AA, 4.5:1 or 3:1 for large text (DEC-6, XP-18), and input boundaries or icons below 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11); text too small to read on a phone, such as body text below 14px; touch targets smaller than KR-3 allows. How to fix: the content items of that list (proof, numbers and promises, the pill, the numbering, the AI sign, competitor claims, service notes, placeholder text) are removed or replaced; restyling one, or turning a pill into a text label, is not a fix. Contrast, size and touch-target defects are restyled (US-012). A fabricated item stays only when the user supplies its source; the one case that waits for the user's answer is the one DEC-5 names. How to check: before judging, list the always-findings and the generic tells and keep them out of the baseline; then list every other element the page uses consistently, each with the places it repeats, and apply an exception only to listed elements. A report that keeps an always-finding as part of the system, or leaves it as an open question, is a finding. Example: a landing page whose monospace captions and plain-text section kickers repeat across its sections keeps them (KR-19, DEC-7), while its "NEW" pill above the headline and an invented "2,400+ teams" are fixed. Not a finding: keeping a consistent pattern that the baseline list names, when it is neither an always-finding nor a generic tell.
rules.title: An existing page is the approved baseline

rules.statement: Fix a defect by changing how the element looks or behaves: its contrast, size, spacing, a shadow or color token, the bounds of its motion, its reduced-motion state. Remove an element only when the element itself is the defect, or when the user asked to remove it. The content always-findings of US-011, such as fabricated proof, a pill above the H1, a service note or placeholder text, are such defects: they are removed or replaced, and restyling them is not a fix. A fix applies in the same way to every element of the same group, or to none of them: removing the border of one link in a list and keeping the borders of the others is a finding. How to check: for each changed element, name the defect by rule ID and the smallest change that removes it; a removal that a restyle would have fixed is a finding, and so is any loss without a named reason. The report ends with a table: element, kept / changed / removed, and the rule ID behind each change. Example: 10px captions raised to a readable size and kept in their typeface; a muted text color darkened until it reaches 4.5:1 instead of removing the text; every row of a link list changed the same way. Not a finding: removing fabricated testimonials (DEC-5); removing an element the user asked to remove.
rules.title: Restyle first, remove last
